Menu.Name: Light Sources
Menu.Label: Configure Light Sources
Menu.Hint: Register items as light sources and configure their light pattern, consumption and duration. GM only.

Compat.Name: System Compatibility
Compat.Label: Configure System Compatibility
Compat.Hint: Choose which of the detected system's item and actor types this module uses, and where an item's quantity is stored. GM only.

Transfer.Name: Import and Export
Transfer.Label: Import or Export Light Sources
Transfer.Hint: Copy this world's light sources and system compatibility settings to a JSON file, or load them from one made in another world. GM only.

AllowFreeForAllDrop.Name: Allow Dropping Free for All Lights
AllowFreeForAllDrop.Hint: Let a lit "Free for All" light be dropped on the ground. No item backs these sources, so dropping one costs nothing and can be repeated without limit. Turn this off to keep free lights on tokens only. A source whose Can Be Dropped is off is never droppable, whatever this setting says.

RestrictPlayerControl.Name: Restrict Light Control to the GM
RestrictPlayerControl.Hint: Only the GM can activate, extinguish, drop or pick up a light source from the Token HUD. Players still see the palette and the lit/unlit state, but their clicks on those controls are refused.

AnnounceLit.Name: Announce Lights in Chat
AnnounceLit.Hint: Post a chat message whenever a light source is lit. Other light events (dropped, picked up, burned out) are unaffected.

Transfer.Title: Import and Export Light Sources
Transfer.ExportHint: Saves this world's light sources, your edits to sources that modules provide, and the system compatibility settings to a JSON file. Sources a module provides are not included: they come back in any world where that module is active.
Transfer.ImportHint: Loads a file exported from another world. Sources in the file replace the ones here with the same item, and the others here are kept. The compatibility settings are applied only when the file comes from the same game system.
Transfer.NoFile: Choose a file to import first.
Transfer.NotAnExport: This file is not a Light Sources export.
Transfer.NoSources: The file holds no light sources.
Transfer.Invalid: Skips {count} that are not valid light sources.
Transfer.Unresolved: These refer to an item that does not exist in this world, so they will only match carried items with the same name and type: {names}.
Transfer.CompatApplied: Replaces the system compatibility settings with the file's.
Transfer.CompatOtherSystem: Keeps this world's system compatibility settings: the file comes from another game system.

Compat.Title: System Compatibility
Compat.SystemNote: Detected system: {system} ({id}). Enable the types this module should treat as light sources and the actors that can carry them.
Compat.ItemsHint: Enable the item types that may be registered as light sources.
Compat.ActorsHint: Enable the actor types allowed to use "free for all" light sources on the Token HUD. Actors carrying a matching light-source item can always use it, regardless of this list.
Compat.NoItemTypes: The active system defines no item types.
Compat.NoActorTypes: The active system defines no actor types.
Compat.QuantityHint: Dotted path to an item's quantity, from the item root (for example: system.quantity). Read by sources that spend a copy, to check availability and to subtract one when lit. Leave empty if the system's items have no quantity — such sources will then never reduce a count.
Compat.ChargesHint: Dotted path to how many charges an item has left, from the item root (for example: system.uses.value). Read by sources that spend a charge, to check availability and, unless a spent path is set below, to subtract one when lit. Leave empty if the system's items have no charges.
Compat.ChargesSpentHint: Optional. For a system that stores the charges used rather than those left (for example: system.uses.spent). When set, lighting adds one here instead of subtracting one from the charges path, which is still what is read.

Fields.SourceNameHint: The exact name an item must have in a character's inventory to count as this light. Renaming changes which items match.
Fields.PatternsHint: Each pattern is a way this light can be lit — for example a wide, short-range beam versus a narrow, long-range one. The actor picks a pattern from the Token HUD. Consumption and duration are shared across every pattern.
Fields.PreviewHint: Select a token on the canvas to preview these settings on it live as you edit. The token's light is restored automatically when you close this window.
Fields.NegativeHint: Sheds darkness instead of light, dimming the area within its radii rather than revealing it. Darkness has its own set of animations, so switching this clears the animation type chosen below.
Fields.AdvancedEnabledHint: Off: the token keeps its own advanced light options, and a dropped light uses Foundry's defaults. On: this pattern sets them, in hand and on the ground. Not available for a darkness source.
Fields.EndingEnabledHint: Off: this pattern keeps the look above until it burns out. On: in its last minutes, as set by Running Low Phase on the Consumption tab, the light takes this look instead — on a token or on the ground, covered or not.
Fields.ConsumeHint: What lighting this source takes from the item. Nothing: the item is the light, like a lantern or a glowing blade. One copy: the item is a stack of identical lights, like five torches; one copy turns into the flame and no longer belongs to the stack. One charge: the item is a single object with uses, like a torch that can be lit three times or a wand with charges; the light burns on that item, goes out when the item leaves the actor, and travels with it when another module carries the item onto the map. A charge put out before it burns down keeps its time on the item, and the next lighting burns that time first without spending another charge. Only lighting spends: switching patterns, dropping and picking up never do.
Fields.CoverableHint: Adds a Stow control beside Drop in the Token HUD, covering the light instead of ending it: it stops shining but keeps burning down, and can be uncovered later with whatever time it has left. Meant for a light that is a spell on an object rather than a flame — a Light cantrip on a pebble is pocketed, not snuffed. Leave off for torches and lanterns.
Fields.DroppableHint: Offers Drop in the Token HUD while the light burns, putting it on the ground as an Ambient Light. Turn off for a light built into what the character wears, like glowing armor or a lamp fixed to a helmet: it stays on the token, and leaves only together with its item when another module carries the item off. Free for All lights also need the Allow Dropping Free for All Lights setting.
Fields.DurationHint: Minutes before the light goes out on its own (counted in the mode chosen below). Use 0 for an unlimited light that only goes out when extinguished manually.
Fields.EndingMinutesHint: How many of the last minutes before the light burns out each pattern shows its Running Low look. Use 0 to turn it off. A value at or above the duration makes the light burn its Running Low look from the moment it is lit.
Fields.DurationModeHint: In-game time: the light burns down as the GM advances the world clock, and stays lit while the clock is still. Real time: the light burns down in real-world minutes even while the game is paused or the owner is offline.
